newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to ease controls on savings/finance firms.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to ease controls on savings/finance firms.

text.p: South Korea's finance ministry said on Friday it would ease regulations on the mutual savings and financing industry, making new entries easier and allowing existing firms to fold.
The government has in practice prevented even shaky firms from folding to protect depositors and has not allowed new entries to protect existing firms, a ministry official said.
"The plan is aimed at boosting operating efficiency of the mutual savings firms through an appropriate level of new entries and departures," a ministry statement said.
The ministry plans to announce further details and criteria early next year, the statement said.
Currently there are 236 mutual savings and financing firms, whose main customers are individuals and self-employed shop owners having difficulty getting loans from commercial banks.
The ministry also said large savings and finance firms would be allowed to convert to provincial banks under certain conditions.
